newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 15.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Northern Irish nationalist party, the SDLP, and the pro-British Ulster Unionist party agreed an agenda on Monday night for the start of substantive peace talks.

- At least one person who contracted the hepatitis C virus from a blood transfusion and a further 28 were not told by the Irish Blood Transfusion Services Board for up to two years that they had the condition.
- Former Irish prime minister Albert Reynolds began his legal battle in London with the Sunday Times newspaper which labelled him a "gombeen man" in an article in 1994.
- Irish financial institution Irish Permanent is close to purchasing the London operation of a state-owned French bank Credit Foncier de France.
- The Irish pound exchange rate dropped below 1.02 sterling for the first time since March 1995.
- Over 1,500 on-stream jobs were announced on Monday in three separate investment projects.

- A surprise deal between the SDLP and UUP last night opened the door for progress at the inter-party political talks at Stormont and appeared to end fears about an imminent breakdown of the loyalist paramiliary ceasefire.
- Increased motor insurance premiums are on the way for 40 percent of Irish motorists after the decision by insurance company Guardian PMPA to increase its rates by five percent from November 1.
- Brixton prison escapee Nessan Quinlivan was among three men being questioned by Irish police on suspicion of IRA membership.
- Yeoman International has acquired the debt of glassware company Tipperary Crystal and has also appointed a receiver.
- A dispute over the way ice-cream is sold in Ireland has broken out again between Irish market leader HB and confectionery company Mars.
- Tony Smurfit said he would work hard to make a success of Smurfit's paper and packaging operation Smurfit France to which he was appointed chief executive on Monday.
